accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the effect of Article 353 during a National Emergency?
o: State Governments are suspended and Parliament directly administers all States.
The Supreme Court assumes the executive functions of the States.
The Governor alone exercises all executive power of the State.
The Centre may give directions to a State on any matter, but State Governments are not suspended.
accepted.x: Article 353 enlarges the executive authority of the Union, enabling it to direct a State on any matter. It does not suspend State Governments.
accepted.tq: Separate the expanded Union power from the false claim that State Governments are abolished.
accepted.sec: National emergency - effects on Centre-State relations (Arts 250, 353, 354)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Article 354, what may the President do during a National Emergency?
o: Transfer all State taxes to the Consolidated Fund of India
Suspend the distribution of all taxes without placing the order before Parliament
Reduce or cancel certain transfers to States until the end of the financial year
Abolish the Finance Commission permanently
accepted.x: Article 354 permits the President to modify or reduce financial transfers during the Emergency, generally until the end of the financial year. The order is required to be laid before Parliament.
accepted.tq: Direct financial-effect question testing the exact scope of Article 354.
accepted.sec: National emergency - effects on Centre-State relations (Arts 250, 353, 354)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following best characterises the federal structure of India during a National Emergency?
o: It becomes more strongly federal because State powers are constitutionally protected.
It remains completely unaffected in legislative, executive and financial spheres.
It becomes confederal, with States acquiring international personality.
It becomes quasi-unitary, with increased powers for the Union.
accepted.x: A National Emergency strengthens the Union and makes the constitutional system operate in a unitary or quasi-unitary manner.
accepted.tq: Use the overall constitutional effect rather than one isolated emergency provision.
accepted.sec: National emergency - effects on Centre-State relations (Arts 250, 353, 354)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: During the operation of a National Emergency, the term of the Lok Sabha may be extended by Parliament by—
o: Five years at a time, with the approval of the Supreme Court
Six months at a time, without any limit
One year at a time, subject to constitutional conditions
Two years at a time, permanently
accepted.x: The term of the Lok Sabha may be extended by Parliament for one year at a time during a National Emergency, subject to the constitutional limitation concerning the period after the Emergency ends.
accepted.tq: Test the exact duration and avoid confusing it with the duration of the Emergency itself.
accepted.sec: National emergency - effects on Centre-State relations (Arts 250, 353, 354)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Article)
a. Article 352
b. Article 356
c. Article 360
List-II (Ground)
i. Threat to financial stability or credit
 ii. War, external aggression or armed rebellion
 iii. Failure of constitutional machinery in a State
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: a-ii, b-iii, c-i
a-iii, b-i, c-ii
a-i, b-ii, c-iii
a-ii, b-i, c-iii
accepted.x: Article 352 concerns war, external aggression or armed rebellion; Article 356 concerns failure of constitutional machinery; and Article 360 concerns financial stability or credit.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure Article-ground pair and eliminate the swapped emergency grounds.
accepted.sec: Emergency types compared - Arts 352, 356, 360  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the three types of emergencies, consider the following statements:
1. Approval of a Proclamation under Article 352 is required within one month.
2. Approval of a Proclamation under Article 356 is required within two months by a special majority.
3. Approval of a Proclamation under Article 360 is required within two months by a simple majority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Article 356 requires approval within two months by a simple majority, not a special majority.
accepted.tq: Spot the wrong majority requirement while retaining the correct time periods.
accepted.sec: Emergency types compared - Arts 352, 356, 360  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated federal consequence of a Financial Emergency under Article 360?
o: The Union may direct States regarding financial propriety.
The Union may direct reduction of salaries and allowances.
The Union automatically assumes all legislative powers of State Legislatures.
Money Bills of States may be required to be reserved for the President's consideration.
accepted.x: Article 360 can enable directions concerning State finances, salary reductions and reservation of State Money Bills. It does not automatically transfer all legislative powers of State Legislatures to the Union.
accepted.tq: Find the overbroad claim that exceeds the financial scope of Article 360.
accepted.sec: Emergency types compared - Arts 352, 356, 360  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states a change introduced by the 44th Constitutional Amendment in relation to National Emergency?
o: It replaced armed rebellion with internal disturbance.
It abolished the requirement of parliamentary approval.
It made Articles 20 and 21 suspendable during every Emergency.
It introduced armed rebellion as a ground and required written advice of the Cabinet.
accepted.x: The 44th Amendment substituted armed rebellion for internal disturbance as a ground and required the Cabinet's advice to be given in writing. It also protected Articles 20 and 21 from suspension.
accepted.tq: Use the amendment-specific changes as a compact constitutional recall test.
accepted.sec: Emergency types compared - Arts 352, 356, 360  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Fundamental Rights remain non-suspendable even during a National Emergency after the 44th Constitutional Amendment?
o: Articles 25 and 26
Articles 20 and 21
Articles 14 and 19
Articles 15 and 16
accepted.x: The 44th Amendment ensured that the protection against conviction for offences under Article 20 and the protection of life and personal liberty under Article 21 cannot be suspended.
accepted.tq: Direct pair-discrimination among neighbouring Fundamental Rights.
accepted.sec: Emergency types compared - Arts 352, 356, 360  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Financial Emergency is correct?
o: It has been used several times since the commencement of the Constitution.
It can be proclaimed only during external aggression.
It has never been used in India.
It automatically dissolves all State Legislative Assemblies.
accepted.x: A Financial Emergency under Article 360 has never been proclaimed in India.
accepted.tq: Test the exceptional historical status of Article 360 without confusing it with Article 356.
accepted.sec: Emergency types compared - Arts 352, 356, 360  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Article 355 imposes on the Union the duty to—
o: Appoint all State ministers during political instability.
Permit States to maintain independent armed forces.
Ensure that every State follows the same social and economic policy.
Protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance and ensure constitutional governance.
accepted.x: Article 355 requires the Union to protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance and to ensure that the government of each State is carried on in accordance with the Constitution.
accepted.tq: Direct duty-and-function question using neighbouring but constitutionally unsupported powers as distractors.
accepted.sec: Union's duty to protect states - Art 355, links to 356 and 365  [other exams]

accepted.s: The constitutional justification most directly associated with the imposition of President's Rule under Article 356 is the Union's duty under—
o: Article 280
Article 393
Article 355
Article 368
accepted.x: The duty imposed on the Union by Article 355 to protect States and ensure constitutional government provides the constitutional basis connected with Article 356 action.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the Union's protective duty and unrelated constitutional provisions.
accepted.sec: Union's duty to protect states - Art 355, links to 356 and 365  [other exams]

accepted.s: Under Article 365, failure by a State to comply with or give effect to directions issued by the Union may be treated as—
o: A breach of parliamentary privilege only
An automatic declaration of Financial Emergency
A reason for terminating the State's representation in Parliament
A ground showing that the government of the State cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution
accepted.x: Article 365 permits failure to comply with Union directions to be treated as evidence of a constitutional breakdown in the State, thereby linking it with Article 356.
accepted.tq: Apply the consequence of disobeying Union directions to the correct constitutional remedy.
accepted.sec: Union's duty to protect states - Art 355, links to 356 and 365  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the subject matter of Part XI of the Constitution?
o: Elections and special provisions for certain classes
Emergency provisions and amendment of the Constitution
Legislative and administrative relations between the Union and the States
Financial relations and trade within India
accepted.x: Part XI contains legislative relations in Articles 245–255 and administrative relations in Articles 256–263 between the Union and the States.
accepted.tq: Part-number and subject matching using the adjacent Part XII as a distractor.
accepted.sec: Constitutional scheme - Parts XI and XII, factors shaping relations  [other exams]

accepted.s: Part XII of the Constitution primarily deals with—
o: Emergency relations between the Union and the States
Financial relations between the Union and the States
Administrative relations between the Union and the States
Inter-State legislative privileges
accepted.x: Part XII deals with financial relations, including Articles 268 to 293.
accepted.tq: Direct Part-subject recall with a Part XI subject as the principal trap.
accepted.sec: Constitutional scheme - Parts XI and XII, factors shaping relations  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a unitary feature of the Indian Constitution?
o: A constitutional prohibition on Union directions to States
Separate and independent judicial systems for the Union and each State
Dual citizenship for Union and State citizens
All India Services serving both the Union and the States
accepted.x: All India Services are a unitary feature because they provide a common administrative structure serving both the Union and the States. India has single citizenship and an integrated judiciary.
accepted.tq: Identify the one genuine unitary feature among reversed or non-existent federal features.
accepted.sec: Constitutional scheme - Parts XI and XII, factors shaping relations  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Governor's office frequently becomes an area of Centre-State friction because the Governor—
o: Is elected directly by the people of the State for a fixed term
Is appointed by the Chief Minister and removable by the Assembly
Is a permanent member of the Union Cabinet
Holds office during the pleasure of the President, under Article 156
accepted.x: The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President under Article 156. Disputes also arise over assent to Bills and addresses to the Legislative Assembly.
accepted.tq: Who-controls-the-office question testing appointment and tenure authority.
accepted.sec: Areas of friction - Governor, 356, fiscal transfers, AIS, river waters, central agencies

accepted.s: Which of the following has been identified as a recurring area of friction concerning Governors?
o: Appointment of judges to the Supreme Court by State Legislatures
Allocation of seats in the Lok Sabha by municipal bodies
Delay in assenting to Bills and issues relating to the address of the Assembly
Determination of the Union Budget by the Governor
accepted.x: Delays in assent to Bills and disputes regarding the Governor's address to the Legislative Assembly are recurring Centre-State friction points.
accepted.tq: Direct issue-identification question focused on the Governor's constitutional role.
accepted.sec: Areas of friction - Governor, 356, fiscal transfers, AIS, river waters, central agencies

accepted.s: President's Rule under Article 356 has been used in India—
o: Exactly 100 times, exclusively with State consent
Only once, in a Union Territory
Fewer than 25 times and only during wartime
More than 125 times, often against governments led by opposition parties
accepted.x: Article 356 has been used over 125 times, and its frequent use against opposition governments has been a major source of Centre-State friction.
accepted.tq: Use the approximate historical frequency and the associated political pattern together.
accepted.sec: Areas of friction - Governor, 356, fiscal transfers, AIS, river waters, central agencies

accepted.s: Why does the exclusion of cesses and surcharges from the divisible pool create friction between the Union and the States?
o: Because cesses and surcharges are constitutionally collected by States.
Because the divisible pool is limited to about 81% of gross tax revenue.
Because States receive the entire gross tax revenue directly.
Because the divisible pool consists only of non-tax revenue.
accepted.x: Cesses and surcharges are excluded from the divisible pool, leaving the pool at approximately 81% of gross tax revenue and reducing the shareable base for States.
accepted.tq: Link the fiscal mechanism to its federal consequence rather than choosing an absolute claim.
accepted.sec: Areas of friction - Governor, 356, fiscal transfers, AIS, river waters, central agencies

accepted.s:
Match the following areas of Centre-State friction with the relevant constitutional or statutory reference:
List-I
 a. Inter-State river-water disputes
 b. Consent for CBI investigation
 c. Governor's tenure
List-II
 i. Section 6 of the DSPE Act
 ii. Article 156
 iii. Article 262
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: a-iii, b-i, c-ii
a-i, b-ii, c-iii
a-ii, b-iii, c-i
a-iii, b-ii, c-i
accepted.x: Article 262 concerns inter-State river-water disputes, Section 6 of the DSPE Act concerns State consent for CBI investigation, and Article 156 concerns the Governor's office.
accepted.tq: Start from the statutory CBI reference and complete the constitutional pairings.
accepted.sec: Areas of friction - Governor, 356, fiscal transfers, AIS, river waters, central agencies

accepted.s:
With reference to the Central Bureau of Investigation, consider the following statements:
1. State consent is required under Section 6 of the DSPE Act.
2. Several States have withdrawn the consent previously granted.
3. The CBI can investigate in every State without any State-related legal limitation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The requirement of State consent means that the CBI does not have an unlimited, State-independent power to investigate in every State.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute claim in statement 3 by applying the consent requirement.
accepted.sec: Areas of friction - Governor, 356, fiscal transfers, AIS, river waters, central agencies

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding GST compensation is correct?
o: GST compensation is constitutionally guaranteed indefinitely without a time limit.
The compensation began only after the 16th Finance Commission.
The compensation promised to States ended in June 2022.
GST compensation was abolished before the GST regime commenced.
accepted.x: The compensation arrangement promised to States under the GST framework ended in June 2022.
accepted.tq: Test the precise end date of a well-known fiscal arrangement.
accepted.sec: Recent friction issues - GST compensation, borrowing, Governor disputes

accepted.s: Kerala v. Union of India (2024) concerned a suit under Article 131 challenging—
o: The appointment of the Governor under Article 156
The distribution of river waters under Article 262
The Net Borrowing Ceiling imposed under Article 293(3)
The validity of GST under Article 279A
accepted.x: Kerala's 2024 suit under Article 131 challenged the Net Borrowing Ceiling imposed under Article 293(3).
accepted.tq: Match the case, constitutional jurisdiction and disputed fiscal provision.
accepted.sec: Recent friction issues - GST compensation, borrowing, Governor disputes

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly reflects recent Governor-related friction in Tamil Nadu and Kerala?
o: The disputes concerned delays in Bills and the skipping of addresses to the Assembly.
The disputes concerned only the appointment of Finance Commission members.
The Governors dissolved Parliament without advice from the Union Council of Ministers.
The States abolished the office of Governor through ordinary legislation.
accepted.x: Recent friction involved delays in dealing with Bills in Tamil Nadu and Kerala and instances where addresses to the Assembly were skipped.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise contemporary issue instead of selecting constitutionally impossible powers.
accepted.sec: Recent friction issues - GST compensation, borrowing, Governor disputes

accepted.s: If Special Category Status had been extended to Andhra Pradesh in the stated form, it would have implied what level of central funding for Centrally Sponsored Schemes?
accepted.x: The proposed Special Category Status would have meant 90% central funding for Centrally Sponsored Schemes.
accepted.tq: Direct percentage recall using progressively higher funding shares as distractors.
accepted.sec: Andhra Pradesh issues - SCS, APRA 2014 assurances, Polavaram funding

accepted.s: Which of the following is included among the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act-related assurances claimed by the opposition to remain unmet?
o: Kadapa steel plant, Dugarajapatnam port and metro rail
Visakhapatnam airport, Kurnool dam and inland waterways
Amaravati High Court, Sriharikota port and a national university only
Polavaram barrage, Hyderabad metro and a new Parliament building
accepted.x: The cited unmet assurances include the Kadapa steel plant, Dugarajapatnam port and metro rail, and were valued at about ₹5 lakh crore by the opposition.
accepted.tq: Use the cluster of named assurances and reject substitutions from nearby infrastructure projects.
accepted.sec: Andhra Pradesh issues - SCS, APRA 2014 assurances, Polavaram funding

accepted.s: A Bill passed by the Lok Sabha provided for Amaravati to be—
o: The sole capital of Andhra Pradesh with effect from 2 June 2024
The temporary capital of Telangana with effect from 2 June 2014
A Union Territory administered by the Governor from 1 January 2025
One of three co-equal capitals with effect from 1 November 1956
accepted.x: The Lok Sabha passed a Bill making Amaravati the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh with effect from 2 June 2024.
accepted.tq: Test the exact status, date and State associated with the capital provision.
accepted.sec: Andhra Pradesh issues - SCS, APRA 2014 assurances, Polavaram funding

accepted.s: Polavaram was declared a national project under which provision of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Section 89
Section 95
Section 108
Section 90
accepted.x: Polavaram is a national project under Section 90 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, and is to be funded entirely by the Centre.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely numbered statutory sections.
accepted.sec: Andhra Pradesh issues - SCS, APRA 2014 assurances, Polavaram funding

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the funding arrangement for the Polavaram national project?
o: It is 100% funded by the Centre.
It is funded only through GST compensation grants.
It is funded 75% by the Centre and 25% by Andhra Pradesh.
It is funded 50% by the Centre and 50% by Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.x: As a national project under Section 90 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, Polavaram is 100% funded by the Centre.
accepted.tq: Direct funding-share question with standard co-financing traps.
accepted.sec: Andhra Pradesh issues - SCS, APRA 2014 assurances, Polavaram funding

accepted.s: Under the Budget 2026–27 provision mentioned for Polavaram, ₹3,320 crore was allocated for storage up to—
o: 35.00 metres
45.72 metres
40.00 metres
41.15 metres
accepted.x: The Budget 2026–27 provision of ₹3,320 crore was for storage up to 41.15 metres, whereas groups demanded funding for the full 45.72 metres.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the funded storage level from the higher level demanded by groups.
accepted.sec: Andhra Pradesh issues - SCS, APRA 2014 assurances, Polavaram funding

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the latest stated position regarding Polavaram funding and progress?
o: ₹12,157 crore has been sanctioned in total; the project was 89% complete and targeted for dedication by March 2027.
₹3,320 crore has been sanctioned in total; the project was 41.15% complete and targeted for dedication by June 2026.
₹45,720 crore has been sanctioned in total; the project was 100% complete and dedicated in 2024.
₹5 lakh crore has been sanctioned in total; the project was 50% complete and targeted for dedication by March 2028.
accepted.x: The stated figures are total sanctions of ₹12,157 crore, 89% completion and a target for dedication by March 2027.
accepted.tq: Combine three numerical facts and reject options that swap an allocation figure for the total sanction.
accepted.sec: Andhra Pradesh issues - SCS, APRA 2014 assurances, Polavaram funding

accepted.s: Which committee has been associated with the call for a “structural reset” of federalism?
o: Punchhi Committee
Sarkaria Committee
Rajamannar Committee of Andhra Pradesh
Kurian Joseph Committee of Tamil Nadu
accepted.x: The Tamil Nadu Kurian Joseph Committee was associated with the call for a structural reset of federalism.
accepted.tq: Direct committee-identification question using familiar Centre-State committees as distractors.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following best captures the Andhra Pradesh-specific federal grievances identified in relation to Centre-State relations?
o: Only the appointment of municipal commissioners and the creation of new districts
Special Category Status and Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act assurances, with Polavaram as a flagship central commitment
Exclusive control over the Union List and abolition of the Finance Commission
Withdrawal from the GST Council and establishment of an independent currency
accepted.x: For Andhra Pradesh, the principal federal grievances are the demand for Special Category Status and implementation of assurances under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act. Polavaram represents a major central commitment.
accepted.tq: Synthesize the State-specific issues without extending them into constitutionally impossible demands.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
